t.1.152.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Terrified by that sound, the people of that Rākṣasa then rushed out of the house, O king, together with their attendants.
t.1.152.2: Those Rākṣasas, terrified and bereft of their senses, mighty Bhīma, best of warriors, comforted, and he bound them to an agreement.
t.1.152.4: Having heard those words of his, O Bhārata, those Rākṣasas said to him, "So be it," and they accepted that compact.
t.1.152.3: "Humans must never again be harmed by you here at any time, for those who do harm shall swiftly meet death in just this same way."
t.1.152.5: From that time on, O Bhārata, the Rākṣasas there were seen to be gentle in that city by the men who dwelt in the city.
t.1.152.6: Then Bhīma took up that lifeless man-eater, threw him down at the gateway, and went away unnoticed.
t.1.152.7: Then Bhīma, having killed him, went to that brahmin's house and told the king everything, in full, just as it had happened.
t.1.152.8: Then, early in the morning, the men who had come out of the city saw the Rākṣasa lying slain on the ground, drenched in blood.
t.1.152.10: Then, O king, the men who dwelt in the city came there by the thousands to see Baka, together with their women, old people and young children.
t.1.152.9: Then others went to Ekacakrā and spread the news of him, who lay sprawled out like a mountain peak, a fearsome sight.
t.1.152.11: Then, having seen that superhuman deed, they were all amazed, and every one of them worshipped the gods, O lord of the people.
t.1.152.12: Then they reckoned up whose turn it was that day to provide the meal; and having learned it, they all came to that brahmin and asked him about it.
t.1.152.13: Questioned thus many times, and protecting the Pāṇḍavas, that bull among Brahmins then spoke these words to all the townspeople.
t.1.152.14: A certain brahmin of great power, perfected in mantras, saw me weeping together with my kinsmen when I had been ordered to be his food.
t.1.152.15: Having first questioned me about my distress and that of the city, that best of brahmins, after reassuring me, spoke as if smiling.
t.1.152.16: "I shall deliver this food to that evil-souled one, and no fear should be felt on my account," said the mighty one.
t.1.152.17: He took that food and went toward Baka's forest; surely it must be by him that this deed, beneficial to the world, has been done.
t.1.152.18: Then all those brahmins and kṣatriyas, greatly amazed, and the vaiśyas and śūdras, rejoicing, held a festival in honor of Brahman.
t.1.152.19: Then all the country folk came to the city to see that most wondrous thing, and the Pārthas lived on right there.
